title: Madd - al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿāt
description: These lines begin the chapter of madd. The first set of rules pertain to madd in al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿāt (the disjointed letters that begin some suwar).

madd_lazim_sukoon.title: Madd lāzim when followed by a sukūn
madd_lazim_sukoon.description: When a sukūn follows the letter of madd present in one of the ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿāt all the qurra will make madd with ṭūl. This scenario falls into the category of madd lāzim.

examples.verse: examples of madd lazim in disjointed letters
examples.note: Notice how the letter ل when spelled out has a madd (the alif preceeded by fatha) as well as a sukūn on the م

no_madd.title: No elongation when no letter of madd present/lack of hamzah or sukūn
no_madd.description: Some of the ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿāt contain no letter of madd (e.g. ألف), such letters will not be lengthened. Additionaly if a letter that does contain a madd within it is not followed by a hamzah or sukūn no cause of madd is established, therefore it will not be streched beyond the natural elongation.

examples.verse: examples of no  madd in disjointed letters
examples.note: The letter ط consists of a letter of madd (طا) however as it is not followed by a hamzah or sukūn it will not be elongated.

letters_of_lin.title: ع in Sūrah Maryam and Shūrā
letters_of_lin.description: The letters that contain a letter of līn as in the letter ع (which is the only letter that falls into this category) at the beginning of Sūrah Maryam and Shūrā have two options for madd: tawassuṭ or ṭūl and the latter is preferred
